questions.q: What living things that live on the earth did Yahweh tell Moses and Aaron the people of Israel could eat?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses and Aaron to tell the people of Israel they could eat any livestock that completely cloven hooves and rechews partially digested food.

questions.q: Was an animal acceptable to eat if it only had a split hoof or if it only chewed the cud?
questions.a: If an animal possessed only one of the two traits, it was not acceptable to eat.

questions.q: What animals living in the water may be eaten by the people of Israel?
questions.a: The people of Israel may eat anything that lives in the water and has both fins and scales.

questions.q: What kind of birds did Yahweh say the people of Israel should detest and not eat?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the people of Israel should detest and not eat eagles, falcons, hawks, vultures and ravens, owls ostriches and even bats.

questions.q: What kinds of insects could be eaten by the people?
questions.a: Insects that walk on legs above their feet, which they use to leap on the ground, may be eaten by the people.

questions.q: What should the people do to four-legged insects that fly?
questions.a: The people should consider any four-legged insect that swarms to be disgusting and completely unacceptable to eat.

questions.q: What animals that swarm on the ground should the people of Israel consider to be unclean?
questions.a: The weasel, the rat, every kind of large lizard, the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon are unclean.

questions.q: What happens to anything that an unclean animal touches?
questions.a: Anything upon which the body of an unclean animal falls shall be unclean.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about things that crawl on the ground?
questions.a: All the animals that crawl upon the ground on four or more legs are to be considered disgusting and unacceptable to eat.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh say that the people of Israel must be holy?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the people must be holy because he is holy.

commentary.text: What animals were clean and unclean.

—These laws seem to have been intended, 1. As a test of the people's obedience, as Adam was forbidden to eat of the tree of knowledge; and to teach them self-denial, and the government of their appetites. 2. To keep the Israelites distinct from other nations. Many also of these forbidden animals were objects of superstition and idolatry to the heathen. 3. The people were taught to make distinctions between the holy and unholy in their companions and intimate connexions. 4. The law forbad, not only the eating of the unclean beasts, but the touching of them. Those who would be kept from any sin, must be careful to avoid all temptations to it, or coming near it. The exceptions are very minute, and all were designed to call forth constant care and exactness in their obedience; and to teach us to obey. Whilst we enjoy our Christian liberty, and are free from such burdensome observances, we must be careful not to abuse our liberty. For the Lord hath redeemed and called his people, that they may be holy, even as he is holy. We must come out, and be separate from the world; we must leave the company of the ungodly, and all needless connexions with those who are dead in sin; we must be zealous of good works devoted followers of God, and companions of his people.
